title: implement load-scenario-aware batch sensitivity guard
author: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a new rollout guard: Load-Scenario-Aware Batch-Sensitivity Guard. Motivation: We observed regressions that only surface under certain batching patterns or request-shape mixes (e.g., high-variance short requests interleaved with long sequence batched requests). Existing guards that look at global percentiles miss these signal-crossings because aggregation dilutes slice-specific deltas. This PR slices telemetry by batch_size and request_profile, computes per-slice quantile deltas normalized by historical slice variance, applies a Bayesian smoothing step to avoid reacting to under-sampled slices, and adapts per-slice sensitivity thresholds dynamically based on stability. A lightweight probe scheduler injects targeted micro-bursts into under-sampled slices to improve confidence for rare but important operating points. The guard integrates with the canary controller to emit soft-rollbacks when a calibrated confidence score exceeds 95% and supports manual override and gradual throttled rollbacks. Includes performance model calibration tooling, integration tests with synthetic multi-batch traces, and dashboard panels for slice heatmaps.

review_conversation: Omar Rahman: Nice direction. Can you clarify how the Bayesian smoothing handles slices with <100 samples? We need to avoid false positives from tiny sample noise.

Maya Chen: Response: smoothing uses an empirical Bayes prior derived from historical inter-slice variance. For slices <100 we bias toward the global prior and increase probe frequency. Added comments and a unit test to validate behavior.
Priya Nair: The probe scheduler looks powerful but could affect production load. Please add circuit-breakers and rate caps so probes cannot exceed N% of traffic per target pool.
Maya Chen: Added rate cap config (charts values) and default hard limit at 0.5% of steady-state QPS per pool. Also added an opt-out flag for enterprise customers that require zero injected traffic.
Liam Gallagher: Integration tests look flaky locally due to timing assumptions. Suggest replacing wall-clock sleeps with virtual clock in tests.
Maya Chen: Updated tests to use test clock harness and reduced flakiness; CI run passes.
Omar Rahman: Approving after CI green and tests stabilized.
Priya Nair: Approved. Left a minor style nit for variable naming which was fixed in follow-up commit.
